channel.description: Latest articles from CT News Junkie (ctnewsjunkie.com)

item.title: Statehouse Partners Adds Pescatello To Team
item.description: Paul Pescatello, formerly senior counsel at the CBIA and executive director of the Connecticut Bioscience Growth Council, has joined Statehouse Partners as a lobbyist, according to the firm.

item.title: As CT Digs Out, More Snow Could Be On The Way
item.description: As Connecticut digs out from a major winter storm that dumped as much as two feet of snow in places, more snow could be coming in a series of storms later this week and early next week, according to early forecasts.

item.title: Energy Committee Hears From CT Officials On Aquarion Water Sale Bill
item.description: The bill, House Bill 7249, would affirm the legislature’s intent that PURA exercise review power over change in control of a water company. Backers hope to pass the legislation before PURA convenes again next month.

item.title: West Hartford Teen Succumbs to Injuries Sustained in Weekend Shooting
item.description: Hartford Police Lt. Aaron Boisvert said in a news release on Sunday that the shooting happened at approximately 1:49 a.m. on Feb. 22, in the vicinity of 181 Ann [Uccello] Street. That area is located just outside PeoplesBank Arena.

item.title: Blumenthal Visits Ukraine, Plus CT Residents Send Aid
item.description: It’s been four years since Russia invaded Ukraine. Peace talks have thus far failed. The war has displaced millions and killed thousands of civilians. U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal spoke to Where We Live about his recent visit to Ukraine. And Connecticut residents have been sending aid overseas.

item.title: Lamont Directs State Flags To Half-Staff In Honor Of Late Civil Rights Leader
item.description: In accordance with the directive, flags will be at half-staff on the Connecticut State Capitol building and all other state-operated buildings, grounds, and facilities statewide. Individuals, businesses, schools, municipalities, and any other private entities and government subdivisions are encouraged to lower their flags for this same duration of time.

item.title: Hospitals Fighting Measles Confront A Challenge: Few Doctors Have Seen It Before
item.description: As the number of cases grows to about 1,000 in the Carolinas, health care workers who’ve never seen the vaccine-preventable disease can get caught by surprise.

item.title: Camp Safety Bill Advances Out Of Committee
item.description: The Committee on Children on Tuesday voted to advance a bill meant to improve safety at municipal-run youth camps in Connecticut.

item.title: CT Joins Lawsuit Against CDC Vaccine Changes
item.description: The lawsuit challenges a January 5, 2026 CDC "Decision Memo" that stripped seven childhood vaccines — those protecting against rotavirus, meningococcal disease, hepatitis A, hepatitis B, influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) — of their universally recommended status.

item.title: Senate Republicans Decry Emergency Bills Expected To Pass Senate
item.description: Senate Democrats defended the action, saying the state would benefit actions such as strengthening election security, empowering workers and ensuring the bottle redemption system was sustainable.
